articles.tag: SEPTIC SHOCK; ENDOTHELIOPATHY; NITRIC OXIDE BIOMARKERS; ILOPROST
articles.title: Effects of Iloprost on Nitric Oxide Biomarkers in Patients With Septic Shock and Severe Endotheliopathy.
articles.dek: A randomized sub-study found that iloprost infusion did not significantly alter plasma nitric oxide biomarkers in critically ill patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy.
summary: This was a preplanned sub-study of the COMBAT-SHINE randomized controlled trial involving 274 adult ICU patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy (defined by soluble thrombomodulin >10 ng/mL). Participants received either a 72-hour intravenous infusion of iloprost (1 ng/kg/min) or placebo. Plasma concentrations of four nitric oxide-related biomarkers—ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine—were measured at baseline, 24, 48, and 72 hours.

In exploratory analyses, iloprost treatment compared with placebo did not produce statistically significant changes in ADMA (−4%, 95% CI: −13% to 6%), SDMA (−2%, 95% CI: −14% to 10%), arginine (9%, 95% CI: −6% to 27%), or homoarginine (17%, 95% CI: −3% to 42%). No significant differences between groups were observed in biomarker trajectories across any time interval (0–24 h, 24–48 h, or 48–72 h), and findings remained consistent in predefined subgroup analyses.

The investigators concluded that iloprost at the tested dose did not measurably affect the studied nitric oxide biomarkers in this septic cohort. These results are presented as exploratory and do not establish whether iloprost affects clinically relevant outcomes in septic shock or whether different dosing or patient populations might show different biomarker responses.
articles.why: Septic shock involves endothelial dysfunction linked to dysregulation of prostacyclin and nitric oxide pathways. This work provides biomarker-level evidence that iloprost did not modulate the specific NO pathway metrics examined, which may inform mechanistic understanding of iloprost's effects (or lack thereof) in severe sepsis. The findings could guide future investigation into whether alternative approaches or biomarkers better capture iloprost's physiologic activity in this population, or whether the agent's clinical utility lies outside NO pathway modulation.
articles.evidence: Randomized, blinded sub-study of a larger trial (COMBAT-SHINE); sample size n=274 (5 participants from the full trial withdrew consent, though the exact final sub-study n is not explicitly restated). Measurements at four timepoints over 72 hours. Major limitations include: results explicitly designated as exploratory rather than confirmatory; no power calculation for the sub-study reported; long-term clinical outcomes and mortality are not addressed in this abstract; causality regarding iloprost's effects on endothelial dysfunction cannot be inferred from biomarker data alone; and uncertainty remains whether measured biomarkers capture all relevant NO pathway activity.

articles.title: Gut microbiome-based interventions to prevent ICU-acquired infections: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.dek: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that selective digestive decontamination and biotic supplementation showed similarly modest protective associations with infection prevention in ICU patients, but neither significantly reduced mortality.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared two opposing gut microbiome-based strategies for preventing ICU-acquired infections: selective digestive decontamination (SDD), which uses antibiotics to eliminate potential pathogens, and biotic supplementation (prebiotics, probiotics, or synbiotics), which aims to enrich beneficial microbes. The authors searched PubMed for randomized controlled trials published between 2000 and 2025 involving adult ICU patients who received either intervention or standard care/placebo, with outcomes including mortality and infection-related events.

Nine SDD trials (19,907 subjects) and 29 biotic supplementation trials (5,483 subjects) were included. Neither SDD nor biotics significantly reduced overall mortality compared to standard care or placebo (SDD: RR = 0.96; biotics: RR = 0.93). Both interventions showed similarly promising but modest protective associations with infections: SDD was associated with modestly lower risk for all-cause ICU-acquired infections (RR = 0.76) compared to biotics (RR = 0.82), and both showed protective associations with pneumonia specifically (SDD: RR = 0.50; prebiotics and synbiotics: RR = 0.70).

The authors conclude that while neither intervention provided mortality benefit, both demonstrated similarly promising protective associations with infection prevention, particularly pneumonia. Substantial heterogeneity exists among biotic trials, limiting confidence in comparative conclusions.
articles.why: This synthesis is relevant to ICU care discussions because it characterizes two fundamentally different microbiome-based approaches within a single evidence framework. The findings suggest that infection prevention—rather than mortality reduction—may be a realistic expectation from these interventions. The comparable effect sizes despite opposite mechanisms may inform clinical discussions about preference between antibiotic-based decontamination and microbial supplementation strategies, though the lack of head-to-head trials and high heterogeneity limit definitive recommendations.
articles.evidence: Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Sample sizes: 19,907 subjects in SDD trials; 5,483 subjects in biotic trials. Major limitations and uncertainties: (1) No randomized trials directly comparing SDD and biotics; (2) High heterogeneity reported, especially among biotic intervention studies, which limits confidence in pooled estimates; (3) Abstract does not specify methodological quality assessment criteria, risk of bias evaluation, or publication bias assessment; (4) Confidence intervals for infection outcomes overlap substantially between interventions, suggesting no statistically significant difference; (5) The 95% confidence interval for overall mortality in biotics narrowly excludes 1.0, introducing uncertainty about true effect direction.

articles.title: Effect of Cysteamine on 90-Day Mortality in Patients With Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.dek: A small randomized trial found no definitive evidence that intravenous cysteamine reduces 90-day mortality in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia, though observed mortality was numerically lower with treatment.
summary: REMAP-CAP is an international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple interventions in community-acquired pneumonia. Adults requiring respiratory or cardiovascular organ support were randomized to intravenous cysteamine (5 mg/kg every 8 hours for up to 10 days) or control. The trial was stopped early for operational futility before reaching predefined statistical thresholds.

Among 36 enrolled patients (19 cysteamine, 17 control), 90-day all-cause mortality was 26% in the cysteamine group versus 35% in the control group (odds ratio 0.64, 95% credible interval 0.18–2.19). One serious adverse event was reported and deemed unrelated to cysteamine. The posterior probability of benefit was 76%.

The authors conclude that these preliminary findings suggest possible benefit but acknowledge that the small sample size prevents definitive conclusions about cysteamine efficacy. They recommend further studies in severe pneumonia. The wide credible interval and early stopping reflect substantial uncertainty about the treatment effect.
articles.why: Cysteamine has theoretical antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antibiotic-potentiating properties that could address multiple pathways in severe pneumonia. Early signals of mortality reduction, even if uncertain, may warrant consideration for future research design. However, the preliminary nature of these data means clinical decisions should not be based on this trial alone.
articles.evidence: Randomized controlled trial design using Bayesian logistic regression. Sample size was 36 patients total. Major limitations include small enrollment, early stopping for operational (not statistical) futility, wide credible interval crossing the null effect, and inability to determine whether observed numerical differences reflect true treatment effects or chance variation. No information is provided about trial registration, baseline characteristics, or mechanisms of the serious adverse event. The small sample precludes robust efficacy assessment.

articles.title: Cross-protective immune responses to pneumococcal serotype 6A following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.dek: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that pneumococcal conjugate vaccines containing serotype 6B elicit measurable cross-reactive immune responses against the related serotype 6A, with stronger responses observed after booster vaccination.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined immune responses to serotype 6A following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines, relevant to India's pneumococcal disease burden from serogroup 6. The authors searched multiple databases for studies reporting serotype 6A-specific IgG concentrations, proportions achieving protective antibody thresholds (≥0.35 µg/mL), and functional opsonophagocytic activity titers. Forty-three studies met inclusion criteria; eight contributed quantitative data for pooled analysis.

Vaccination with 6B-containing vaccines produced measurable cross-reactive IgG and functional immune responses against serotype 6A. Schedules including a booster dose (3 + 1) showed numerically higher responses than those without a booster (3 + 0): pooled IgG geometric mean concentrations of 1.63 versus 0.59 µg/mL, proportions achieving IgG ≥0.35 µg/mL of 92.78% versus 65.38%, and opsonophagocytic activity geometric mean titers of 984.6 versus 169.2, respectively.

These findings suggest that 6B-mediated cross-protective responses occur against serotype 6A, particularly following booster dosing in vaccinated children. However, interpretation requires consideration of the small number of studies contributing quantitative data and the range of methodologies employed across included studies.
articles.why: Cross-protective immunity between related pneumococcal serotypes could inform vaccine strategy discussion and serotype coverage assessment in populations with high pneumococcal disease burden. Understanding the magnitude and durability of cross-reactive responses may help contextualize observed clinical effectiveness of current vaccine schedules and guide future vaccine recommendations, particularly regarding booster timing.
articles.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational and interventional studies. Total sample size not reported in the abstract. Only 8 of 43 included studies contributed quantitative data for meta-analysis, suggesting substantial heterogeneity and limited pooled data. Study designs, age groups, vaccine types, and measurement methodologies across included studies are not detailed in the abstract. The abstract does not report confidence intervals, statistical significance testing, or heterogeneity measures. Registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251134118).

articles.title: Nebulized interferon-β1a (SNG001) in COVID-19 patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.dek: A meta-analysis of four randomized controlled trials found that nebulized interferon-β1a reduced COVID-19 hospitalizations and serious adverse events, though it did not affect mortality or recovery rates.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled data from four randomized controlled trials comparing nebulized interferon-β1a (SNG001) with placebo or standard care in COVID-19 patients, enrolling 1,055 participants total. The review searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and clinicaltrials.gov through November 2025 without language restrictions.

SNG001 was associated with significantly fewer hospitalizations (risk ratio 0.16, 95% CI 0.03–0.88, from two trials) and fewer serious adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.47–0.90). No statistically significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.72), non-recovery at day 28 (RR 0.87), or adverse events overall (RR 0.97).

The authors concluded that nebulized SNG001 was safe and potentially beneficial for outpatient COVID-19 treatment, particularly regarding hospital admission reduction. However, they emphasized the need for larger trials, especially in vaccinated and previously infected populations, before firm clinical recommendations can be made.
articles.why: This finding may inform discussions about early outpatient COVID-19 interventions, particularly in clinical settings managing high-risk patients at risk of hospitalization. The apparent reduction in serious adverse events and hospitalizations—without harm signals—could support consideration of SNG001 in treatment protocols. However, the absence of mortality benefit and the limited number of included trials underscore that this represents preliminary evidence requiring confirmation in larger populations.
articles.evidence: Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Sample size: 1,055 participants across four RCTs. Major limitations: Only two trials provided hospitalization data, limiting precision of that estimate. No mortality benefit detected, suggesting SNG001 may not reduce the most severe outcomes. Generalizability uncertain in vaccinated and previously infected cohorts, as noted by authors. Full-text assessment not conducted in this briefing.

articles.tag: VASCULAR ASSESSMENT; GESTATIONAL HYPERTENSION; PREECLAMPSIA; POSTPARTUM CARDIOVASCULAR RISK
articles.title: Non-invasive vascular assessment in gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period: a systematic review.
articles.dek: A systematic review of 49 studies finds that non-invasive vascular imaging techniques can detect structural and functional abnormalities in blood vessels during and after pregnancies complicated by gestational hypertension or preeclampsia, though their value for predicting future cardiovascular disease remains uncertain.
summary: This systematic review searched five major databases through May 2024 for studies using non-invasive vascular assessment methods—including pulse-wave velocity, carotid intima-media thickness, flow-mediated dilation, ophthalmic artery Doppler, and retinal imaging—in pregnant or postpartum women. The analysis included 49 studies involving 32,683 participants. Due to heterogeneous study designs and methods, findings were synthesized narratively rather than meta-analytically.

Women with gestational hypertension showed consistent signs of arterial stiffness (elevated pulse-wave velocity and augmentation index), reduced endothelial function (decreased flow-mediated dilation), and increased carotid intima-media thickness during pregnancy and postpartum. Some vascular abnormalities persisted from weeks to years after delivery, and retinal imaging detected altered vessel caliber in some women up to six years postpartum. Ophthalmic artery Doppler findings were more variable across studies.

The authors conclude that non-invasive vascular assessment can identify macrovascular, microvascular, and endothelial dysfunction in women with hypertensive pregnancy disorders. However, they note that evidence is currently insufficient to use these measurements as independent predictors of future cardiovascular events. Standardized, prospective longitudinal studies with consistent methodology are needed to establish clinical and prognostic value.
articles.why: This review highlights an important gap: women with gestational hypertension and preeclampsia face elevated long-term cardiovascular risk, yet current clinical practice lacks validated biomarkers to identify high-risk individuals for preventive intervention. The persistence of vascular abnormalities after pregnancy suggests that pregnancy-related hypertension may unmask underlying vascular dysfunction. Understanding which vascular assessment techniques best predict cardiovascular outcomes could inform postpartum surveillance strategies and risk stratification, though the review makes clear that individual test results cannot currently guide clinical decisions.

evidence.design: Systematic review of observational studies (design types not fully specified in abstract)
major_limitations: Substantial heterogeneity in study design, methodology, and measurement protocols prevented pooled meta-analysis
Inconsistent findings across studies, particularly for ophthalmic artery Doppler
No data provided on study quality assessment or risk of bias
Abstract does not specify follow-up duration for individual studies or whether cohort studies were prospective or retrospective
No effect sizes, confidence intervals, or statistical comparisons reported
Insufficient evidence stated by authors regarding use as independent cardiovascular predictors

articles.title: Apixaban reduces hepatic decompensation in patients with cirrhosis (ApiHep): A randomized controlled trial.
articles.dek: A randomized controlled trial found that apixaban, a direct oral anticoagulant, reduced hepatic decompensation in patients with moderate-to-advanced cirrhosis without increasing bleeding risk over one year.
summary: This open-label randomized controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment enrolled 134 adults (ages 18–60) with cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B or C stage, excluding those with splenoportal axis thrombosis). Participants were randomly assigned to receive either apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily plus standard medical therapy (n=67) or standard medical therapy alone (n=67) for 12 months.

Patients receiving apixaban experienced significantly lower rates of hepatic decompensation (33.1% vs. 54.3%; absolute risk reduction 21.2%, p=0.013). Secondary outcomes—including ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and variceal bleeding—showed numerically lower rates in the apixaban group but did not reach statistical significance. No significant differences in all-cause or liver-related mortality were detected. Adverse events, any bleeding, and major bleeding occurred at similar rates between groups (55.2% vs. 53.7%, 41.8% vs. 46.3%, and 9.0% vs. 11.9%, respectively).

These findings suggest anticoagulation with apixaban may help prevent clinical decompensation in patients with moderate-to-advanced cirrhosis without an apparent increase in hemorrhagic complications. However, the trial does not establish whether apixaban improves survival or defines optimal patient selection, and the generalizability beyond the enrolled age range (18–60 years) remains uncertain.
articles.why: The traditional concern that anticoagulation worsens bleeding in cirrhosis may not apply uniformly to all direct oral anticoagulants or patient groups. If confirmed in larger studies, apixaban could inform discussions about managing thrombotic risk and preventing decompensation in select cirrhosis patients. This work contributes to evolving evidence on anticoagulation safety in advanced liver disease but should not direct individual clinical decisions without review of the complete literature and patient factors.
articles.evidence: Randomized controlled trial (blinded endpoint assessment); n=134 (67 per group). Major limitations include open-label design for treatment allocation, restriction to ages 18–60 (limiting applicability to older patients), exclusion of those with splenoportal axis thrombosis, and lack of mortality benefit at one year. The abstract does not provide information on trial registration date, follow-up completion rates, baseline imbalances, or subgroup analyses. Uncertainty persists regarding durability beyond 12 months, long-term safety, and applicability to other oral anticoagulants.

articles.tag: ALCOHOL-ASSOCIATED LIVER DISEASE; TRANSIENT ELASTOGRAPHY; ABSTINENCE
articles.title: Alcohol abstinence and liver stiffness by vibration-controlled transient elastography: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.dek: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies found that liver stiffness measured by transient elastography decreases within 7 days of alcohol cessation but shows modest overall improvement, while relapse is associated with increases in stiffness.
summary: This systematic review searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases from 1996 to 2024 for studies with paired vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) measurements in adults who stopped drinking or relapsed. Eleven studies comprising 1,557 patients met inclusion criteria. VCTE is a non-invasive ultrasound technique that measures liver stiffness as a proxy for fibrosis and inflammation.

In patients who remained abstinent, mean liver stiffness decreased by 1.95 kPa at 7 days, 2.30 kPa at 30 days, and 2.76 kPa after 56 days (pooled effect size −0.13 SD units). The most substantial change occurred early: the first week showed significant reduction (−0.21 SD units), while later follow-up showed minimal additional improvement (−0.11 SD units, not statistically significant). Conversely, patients who relapsed showed increases in liver stiffness: +0.86 kPa at 30 days and +0.40 kPa after 56 days (pooled effect size +0.18 SD units).

These directionally opposite changes in liver stiffness with abstinence versus relapse align with the concept of alcohol-associated inflammatory liver injury. However, the authors note uncertainty about whether these stiffness changes correlate with actual histologic fibrosis, since the studies did not include paired liver biopsy data to validate the elastography findings.
articles.why: Alcohol-associated liver disease represents a major cause of preventable liver morbidity and mortality, and understanding the trajectory of liver injury reversal could inform discussions with patients about the timing and expected benefits of abstinence. The finding of rapid early improvement in liver stiffness may provide patients with objective feedback during the critical early period of alcohol cessation. The apparent plateau after 7 days and the increase with relapse underscore the importance of sustained abstinence. However, the modest absolute changes and uncertainty about their relationship to true fibrosis progression mean these measurements should be interpreted cautiously and not as standalone indicators of liver health.
articles.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 observational studies (n=1,557 patients total) with paired VCTE assessments. The search strategy was comprehensive across major databases over 28 years. Major limitations: (1) the studies included were observational rather than randomized, raising potential for confounding and selection bias; (2) ROBINS-I was used to assess bias, but specific results are not reported in the abstract; (3) the absolute changes in liver stiffness are small and their clinical significance is unclear; (4) no paired histology was available to validate whether stiffness changes reflect true changes in fibrosis; (5) the abstract does not specify follow-up duration ranges, population characteristics, or heterogeneity measures; (6) the mechanism underlying rapid early improvement (inflammation vs. fibrosis reduction) cannot be determined from stiffness measurement alone.

articles.title: Gitelman syndrome complicated by pregnancy: clinical management and maternal-fetal outcomes - a systematic review.
articles.dek: A systematic review of 56 studies examining maternal and fetal complications, management strategies, and outcomes in pregnancies complicated by Gitelman syndrome.
summary: This systematic review, conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searched four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI) through December 31, 2025, for studies of Gitelman syndrome in pregnancy. The analysis included 56 studies reporting 96 pregnancies in 81 women across 19 countries. Data were analyzed descriptively, with categorical variables reported as frequencies and continuous variables as mean ± SD or median (range).

Among pregnancies with available outcome data, maternal complications were reported in some pregnancies: gestational diabetes mellitus (11.5%), oligohydramnios (9.4%), and preeclampsia/HELLP syndrome (3.1%). Fetal and neonatal complications included preterm birth (16.7%), growth restriction (5.2%), and fetal/neonatal death (4.2%). Pregnancies with preconception diagnosis appeared to have lower rates of gestational diabetes (6.3% vs 18.4%) and fetal/neonatal death (0% vs 8.2%), though the authors note these comparisons were descriptive and exploratory only. Oral potassium and magnesium supplementation were primary treatments; potassium-sparing diuretics were used in 16 pregnancies (18 exposures) with no reported malformations, though safety remains unestablished. Vaginal delivery occurred in 51.2% and Cesarean delivery in 48.8%.

The authors conclude that preconception counseling and multidisciplinary care with close electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation may benefit pregnancies with Gitelman syndrome, but evidence is substantially limited by reliance on case-report data, publication bias, and outcome heterogeneity. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed.
articles.why: Gitelman syndrome is a rare genetic disorder affecting electrolyte balance; pregnancy can amplify existing imbalances and potentially increase risks. This review synthesizes scattered case reports to identify complications warranting clinical attention and management approaches. The findings suggest potential value of preconception diagnosis and coordination of care, which may inform counseling discussions with affected women planning pregnancy. However, the limited evidence base means individualized assessment and specialized nephrology/maternal-fetal medicine consultation remain important.
articles.evidence: Systematic review of observational studies (predominantly case reports). Sample: 96 pregnancies from 56 studies in 81 women. Major limitations: (1) evidence drawn almost entirely from case reports with inherent publication and selection bias; (2) heterogeneous reporting of outcomes and management; (3) descriptive analysis without adjusted comparisons or formal statistical testing; (4) apparent comparisons (preconception diagnosis cohorts) are exploratory and not statistically rigorous; (5) no information provided on methodological quality of included studies or assessment of bias; (6) incomplete outcome data for some pregnancies. The safety profile of potassium-sparing diuretics in pregnancy remains unestablished despite 18 exposures reported.

articles.title: Expression of Ki-67 as a Prognostic Marker in Cutaneous Melanoma: A Systematic Review.
articles.dek: A systematic review of 18 studies found that high Ki-67 expression, a marker of cell proliferation, is associated with adverse prognostic features and survival outcomes in cutaneous melanoma, though measurement variability limits definitive conclusions.
summary: This systematic review synthesized evidence from 18 retrospective cohort studies published between January 2000 and December 2024, involving 3622 patients across Europe, China, and the United States. The review examined whether Ki-67 labeling index—a measure of tumor cell proliferation—could predict prognosis in cutaneous melanoma, following standardized systematic review guidelines (PRISMA 2020).

High Ki-67 expression was frequently associated with adverse clinical features including increased Breslow thickness (tumor depth) and lymph node metastasis. In several studies, Ki-67 functioned as an independent predictor of survival, suggesting prognostic value beyond established markers.

The authors concluded Ki-67 warrants consideration as a prognostic marker for melanoma. However, substantial heterogeneity in cutoff values and staining protocols across studies limited comparability. The Quality In Prognosis Studies tool assessment identified low-to-moderate bias risk, with confounding variables and inconsistent biomarker measurement as the most frequent methodological limitations.
articles.why: Ki-67 is routinely available through immunohistochemistry and could potentially enhance prognostic stratification of melanoma patients if standardized protocols were established. This review acknowledges both the promise of Ki-67 as a proliferation marker and the current evidence gaps that prevent its definitive clinical integration alongside established markers like Breslow thickness.
articles.evidence: Design: Systematic review of retrospective cohort studies (n=18 studies, 3,622 patients total). Major limitations: substantial variability in Ki-67 cutoff thresholds and immunostaining methods across studies; inconsistent confounder adjustment; heterogeneity limiting direct comparison of results. No meta-analysis effect sizes reported in abstract. Risk of bias assessed as low-to-moderate overall, but confounding and measurement inconsistency identified as recurring problems.
